title: KV microstrip orchestration for streaming batch fusion across tensor/pipeline parallelism
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: As continuous (streaming) batching behavior grows, current KV cache layout across tensor/pipeline parallel setups leads to uneven GPU memory usage and backpressure during long prefix reuse. This ticket designs and implements a 'microstrip' orchestration layer that shards KV entries at sub-slab granularity and coordinates placement, prefetch, and eviction across pipeline stages and tensor-parallel replicas to improve memory utilization, reduce cross-GPU transfer spikes, and preserve latency SLOs.
background: Current KV strategy shards at slab-level and ties allocation to model tensor/pipeline layout. For large streaming workloads with heterogeneous sequence lengths, this causes hot-slab concentration on some GPUs, frequent cross-device page-in operations, and amplified latencies during continuous batching bursts. Benchmarks (see links) show 18-35% tail latency increase under mixed-length streams on 8-GPU nodes and >12% effective memory fragmentation compared to an ideal packing.
proposal: Introduce a Microstrip KV Orchestrator: a lightweight, deterministic microshard map that splits KV caches into small fixed-size microstrips (e.g., 64KB segments). The orchestrator assigns microstrips across GPUs with an affinity-aware hashing layer that considers: pipeline stage ownership, tensor-parallel replica sets, recent access heat (hotness window), and per-GPU free memory headroom. Key components: (1) Microstrip map service (local in-node coordinator + small raft-less consensus for multi-node), (2) async prefetch scheduler that coalesces microstrips for upcoming tokens in streaming batches, (3) eviction & compaction engine that rebalances microstrips proactively between steps to avoid burst transfers, (4) deterministic fallback mode for Dedicated/Private where cross-host transfers are disallowed.
design_decisions: Microstrip size set to 64KB by default; tunable per-workload via profile
Deterministic mapping uses XOR+affinity salt derived from model id + prefix hash to avoid coordination for most lookups
Coordinator is local to node to avoid cross-host latency; cross-node rebalancing happens asynchronously with per-host quotas
Prefetch is scheduled per-request group (stream) not per-request to enable fusion of microstrips across concurrent streaming batches
Eviction favors cold microstrips first and tries in-node peer transfers before spilling to host memory
tradeoffs: Smaller microstrips reduce fragmentation but increase metadata overhead in map and network messages
Local coordinator reduces lookup RTT but requires eventual consistency guarantees for cross-node reuse which may lead to short-lived misroutes
Aggressive prefetch reduces tail latency but increases peak GPU memory usage during bursts
Deterministic mapping reduces coordination but may under-exploit transient load imbalance without periodic rebalancing

acceptance_criteria: End-to-end correctness: no KV lookup mismatches across tensor/pipeline boundaries after microstrip rollout
Tail latency (p95/p99) for mixed-length streaming traces reduced by >=10% compared to current slab strategy under identical load
Peak GPU memory fragmentation improved: achieve >=8% reduction in unusable reserved memory measured by free-headroom metric
Cross-GPU transfer spikes during continuous batching reduced by >=30% (measured as 1s moving-average of inter-GPU egress bytes)
Feature gated: must be toggleable per-cluster and support deterministic fallback where cross-host movement is disabled
Integration tests for tensor-parallel replica correctness and pipeline stage ownership pass in CI
